    How it works

    Three steps, thirty seconds

    STEP 01

    Drop your export

    Export from CapCut, Premiere or your capture software at the highest quality you have — 4K if you recorded it. Drop the MP4 here.

    STEP 02

    We rebuild the container

    The video and audio streams are copied bit-for-bit. Only the container changes: faststart order, clean metadata, repaired indexes.

    STEP 03

    Post the optimized file

    Download it and upload that file to TikTok. Same clip — presented as a clean, high-bitrate source the pipeline treats gently.

    FAQ

    Straight answers

    Does the optimizer reduce my video quality? +
    No. The video and audio streams are copied bit-for-bit — there is no re-encoding, no downscaling, no bitrate change. Only the MP4 container around those streams is rebuilt. You can verify it yourself: resolution, FPS and bitrate shown after optimizing match the original exactly.
    What does it actually change, then? +
    Three things: the moov atom (the file's index) is moved to the front — the "faststart" layout streaming platforms prefer; junk metadata and dead space (recorder tags, free/skip boxes) are removed; and the chunk offsets inside the index are rewritten so the rebuilt file stays perfectly valid.
    Will TikTok still compress my video? +
    TikTok re-processes every upload on its own servers, and no tool can switch that off — anyone who promises "zero compression, guaranteed" is overselling. What a clean, faststart, high-bitrate container does is give TikTok's pipeline a proper source to work from, which is exactly the case where its lighter-touch processing applies. Creators consistently see visibly sharper results than with a messy raw export.
    Is my video uploaded to a server? +
    Never. The optimizer runs entirely in your browser using the File API — the file is read, rebuilt and downloaded locally on your device. Close the tab and nothing remains anywhere.
    Which files work best? +
    MP4 or MOV files with H.264, HEVC (H.265) or AV1 video. Vertical 1080 × 1920 is TikTok's baseline; 2160 × 3840 (4K vertical) at 60 or 120 FPS with a bitrate of 40 Mbps or more gives the pipeline the most to work with. The analyzer above scores your file on exactly these points.
    Why are there daily limits on Free? +
    The Free tier covers casual posters — 3 videos a day up to 100 MB each. Booster and Premium raise the size and daily caps for creators who post constantly or work with long 4K captures.
    Can you check my video's views or shadow-ban status from its link? +
    No — and neither can anyone else. TikTok's public link data (the oEmbed service our Link Analyzer uses) returns only the title, author and thumbnail. View counts, likes, FPS, codec and any restriction status are not exposed to outside tools, so tools that claim to check them from a link are estimating or inventing numbers. If you want real technical facts about a video, analyze the file — that data is actually in there.
